name: the-accent-theme-reaches-a-rendered-surface
description:
Settings.json says overlayAccent nord, and this asks a REAL overlay surface what it resolved - not what the stylesheet says, and not what the push emitted.

WHY ALL FOUR TOKENS. The criterion is that a theme repaints the surfaces to its OWN values, not only its accent. The brand book's themes differ in ink and paper as much as in accent, so a run that checked --ov-accent alone would pass on half a theme, which reads as wrong rather than as subtle. Nord is #88C0D0 on #ECEFF4 with ink 46 52 64, values the test suite pins to docs/brand/brand-book.html.

WHY THE BRAND CLASS IS CHECKED TOO. html.atrium-overlay-accent-brand pins --ov-accent to the crimson fallback at the same specificity as a theme class, so if both are on the winner is decided by which rule sits later in overlay.css. The push turns the brand one off when a theme is set, and this is what says it actually did.

The choice must survive a restart. The relaunch below reads the same tokens from a second launch against the same staged file, with no click in between.

actions.note: the theme push runs after the document is up

actions.expression: (() => { const r = document.documentElement; const s = getComputedStyle(r); const t = (n) => (s.getPropertyValue(n) || '').trim().toLowerCase(); return 'accent=' + t('--ov-accent') + ' paper=' + t('--ov-paper') + ' soft=' + t('--ov-soft') + ' ink=' + t('--ov-ink') + ' classes=' + [...r.classList].filter((c) => c.startsWith('atrium-')).join(',') ; })()
actions.note: the four tokens and every atrium- class, so a failure names what it got rather than only that it differed
a triplet, not a colour, because it is consumed as rgb(var(--ov-ink) / alpha)
Cmd+Q then Atrium again against the SAME staged settings, with nothing clicked

actions.expression: (() => { const r = document.documentElement; const s = getComputedStyle(r); const t = (n) => (s.getPropertyValue(n) || '').trim().toLowerCase(); return 'accent=' + t('--ov-accent') + ' paper=' + t('--ov-paper') + ' soft=' + t('--ov-soft') + ' ink=' + t('--ov-ink') + ' classes=' + [...r.classList].filter((c) => c.startsWith('atrium-')).join(',') ; })()

assertions.desc: the push put the theme's class on the document
and turned the brand accent class off, so the two are not both pinning --ov-accent at equal specificity
And --ov-paper to Nord's #ECEFF4. Accent alone would pass on half a theme.
A second launch against the same file resolves the same accent, with nothing clicked in between
